properties.statement:
THIRD KNOWN OCCURRENCE, and the first two already have recorded causes. Told that a released version had broken reconnection and pointed at the appended field feedback, the agent read 274 new lines, ran two verification commands, and wrote a cause into a chat message — "This is my fault, and I predicted it" — with the root-cause skill never loaded. Anthony asked whether it had been run. It had not.

WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED, and it bounds this more than anything else: the BRAINSTORM half of the same rule ran correctly TWICE in the same session, each time producing an exploratory Decision with the user's own words, unranked options, a stated counter and a relation drawn with evidence. So this is not a broken skill surface and not an agent that ignores skills. Both brainstorms arrived as `/brainstorm` TYPED BY THE USER. Across the entire session the agent self-invoked ZERO skills.

═══ THE CAUSE WAS ALREADY RECORDED, TWICE ═══

`fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it` (2026-08-28): "Unprompted self-invocation is close to absent." `fact:the-field-feedback-rule-was-broken-the-same-day-it-was-ruled-on...` (2026-09-07) records this same rule broken the same way, with the same bounding observation that the agent had read the rule hours earlier. So the question worth answering is not why it happened again — it is WHY THE FIX BUILT FOR IT DID NOT FIRE.

═══ THE NEW FINDING: THE DEMAND IS DOWNSTREAM OF THE ACT IT GOVERNS ═══

The 2026-09-07 fix was `record_finding`, whose description says GET THE root-cause SKILL FIRST, with `demanded_by: [record_finding]` on the skill. Measured 2026-09-09: **exactly ONE tool of 178 demands any skill at all**, and it is that one.

⭐ BUT `record_finding` IS THE TOOL YOU CALL TO RECORD A CAUSE — it is reached AFTER the cause has been formed. The skill's own trigger is "the moment you are about to write down a cause", and a cause is most often first written as PROSE TO THE USER, which passes through no tool at all. There is nothing between the agent and a sentence in a chat message. **So the enforcement point sits strictly downstream of the moment it exists to catch**, and would have been missed on this occurrence even with the tool available.

THE TOOL WAS ALSO ABSENT, which is a second and independent failure of the same mechanism: the reflow2 MCP client was disconnected for this entire session, so no `mcp__reflow2__*` tool existed in the agent's surface. The demand mechanism is a tool description, and the incident under investigation WAS the tool surface being down. **A demand carried on a tool cannot fire in the class of incident where the tools are what broke** — and a field report about reflow2 failing to connect is exactly that class.

═══ AND THE GATE THAT WATCHES THIS WAS GREEN THROUGHOUT ═══

`skill_lint` checks that a skill naming `demanded_by` is demanded back by that tool's description. It passed on every run today, through both the omission and the incident. It verifies THE DECLARATION IS PRESENT; it cannot see whether the demand ever fires. That is the same class as the defect this session was called in to investigate — the version guard refusing on a schema STAMP rather than on the POPULATION it claims to protect. **Two instances of "a declaration was read as evidence about behaviour" in one incident, one in the product and one in its own enforcement.**

═══ ALSO MEASURED ═══

`rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed` carries NO `enforcement` value at all — the field is unset, so nobody has ruled on whether breaking it should fail anything. It has been broken on two of the two field reports since it was written.

═══ WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED (step 9) ═══

Whether the agent would have loaded the skill had `record_finding` been available. It is UNTESTABLE from here and the two candidates predict the same observation on this occurrence: the tool was absent AND the cause was formed before any tool call, so neither can be separated by what happened. Naming which dominates would need an occurrence with the tools up, and that is worth waiting for rather than guessing.

Also not established: whether any enforcement point could exist upstream of prose. Nothing observable fires on "an agent is about to explain something", which the skill's own text says about itself — so this may be a cause with no mechanical fix, and saying so is more useful than proposing one that would sit downstream again.
